::: {style="color: #97BC62; font-size: 1rem; margin-top: 1rem;"}
Definition, classification, and why it matters for Pakistan
:::

---

## Services create value without producing a physical good — and they drive Pakistan's modern economy

- **Definition:** Services are intangible economic activities — banking, retail, transport, education, health, ICT — where output is consumed as it is produced

- **Also called the Tertiary Sector;** it follows from agriculture (primary) and manufacturing (secondary) in the structural transformation ladder

- **PBS classifies services into:** Wholesale & Retail Trade · Transport & Storage · ICT · Finance & Insurance · Real Estate · Public Administration · Education · Health · Other Private Services

- **Services differ from goods in four ways —** Intangibility (cannot be touched), Inseparability (produced and consumed simultaneously), Variability (quality varies), and Perishability (cannot be stored)

::: {.source-line}
Source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, National Accounts Methodology; Ministry of Finance
:::

---

## Pakistan's IT and telecom sectors are growing rapidly — but remain far below their potential

- **Telecom:** ~200 million subscriptions by March 2025; sector revenues Rs 803 billion (Jul–Mar FY25); mobile data usage jumped 68.9% YoY to 4.3 GB per subscriber

- **IT Exports:** Reached ~$3.2 billion annually; Pakistan ranks among the world's top-5 freelancing nations by earnings

- **Startups:** Over 1,900 startups incubated under National Incubation Centres (NICs); 185,000+ jobs created; Rs 30.8 billion in investments; 12,000 women entrepreneurs empowered

- **Government Push:** e-Rozgaar targeting 50 active centres by FY2025; China–Pakistan JWG for ICT, cybersecurity, and 5G cooperation

- **Constraint:** High duties on mobile devices, rupee depreciation (−17% in 2024) inflating spectrum fees, and limited 5G rollout throttle competitiveness

::: {.source-line}
Source: Pakistan Economic Survey 2024–25; SBP; Mordor Intelligence Telecom Pakistan Report 2026
:::

---

## Banking is modernising fast — but financial exclusion leaves most Pakistanis outside the formal economy

- **Finance & Insurance** contribute ~4% of GDP but function as the nerve centre of investment, credit, and economic confidence

- **SBP cut policy rates** by 450 basis points to 17.5% through FY2025 — easing credit and spurring private investment growth of 9.9%

- **Mobile banking surge:** JazzCash alone has 48 million registered wallets; mobile banking transactions hit 1.69 billion in FY2025 — financial inclusion from the bottom up

- **Capital markets:** PSX market capitalisation surged 50% to Rs 10.2 trillion; KSE-100 gained 78,000 points; corporate bond issuance up 38% to Rs 480 billion

- **Key gap:** Only ~35% of adults hold bank accounts; 72% of non-agricultural workers are in the informal economy without access to credit, insurance, or pensions

::: {.source-line}
Source: Pakistan Economic Survey 2024–25; SBP Annual Report; Express Tribune June 2025
:::

---

## Pakistan's services sector is split: a growing formal economy alongside a vast informal one

```{=html}
<div class="two-col-contrast">
  <div class="contrast-left">
    <div class="col-label-green">Formal Services (Registered &amp; Taxed)</div>
    <ul style="font-size:0.83rem; line-height:1.8; color:#3E3E3E; padding-left:1.2rem;">
      <li>Banks, telecom firms, listed companies</li>
      <li>Pays taxes, counted fully in GDP</li>
      <li>Regulated by SBP, SECP, PTA</li>
      <li>Workers have contracts, benefits, pensions</li>
      <li>Accessible to foreign investment &amp; credit</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="contrast-right">
    <div class="col-label-brown">Informal Services (Unregistered &amp; Untaxed)</div>
    <ul style="font-size:0.83rem; line-height:1.8; color:#3E3E3E; padding-left:1.2rem;">
      <li>Street vendors, informal retail, rickshaws</li>
      <li>Largely invisible to GDP measurement</li>
      <li>No regulatory oversight or consumer protection</li>
      <li>Workers lack social safety nets</li>
      <li><strong>72.1% of non-agricultural employment</strong> — the majority</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="source-line">Source: Labour Force Survey 2024–25; Wikipedia Economy of Pakistan 2025; Bank of Scotland Trade 2024</div>
```

## Six structural barriers prevent Pakistan's services sector from reaching its full potential

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 0.4rem;">
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle">1</div>
    <div class="row-title">Low Tax Base</div>
    <div class="row-desc">Services = 58% of GDP but contribute a disproportionately small share of taxes — most providers operate outside the formal tax net</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle brown">2</div>
    <div class="row-title">Skills Gap</div>
    <div class="row-desc">Education spending is only 2.1% of GDP (UNESCO benchmark: 4–5%); workforce skills do not match what services employers need</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle">3</div>
    <div class="row-title">Digital Divide</div>
    <div class="row-desc">Internet growth is uneven — rural areas and women remain largely excluded from digital services, e-commerce, and online work</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle rust">4</div>
    <div class="row-title">Energy Crisis</div>
    <div class="row-desc">Utility tariffs rose 29% in FY2025; erratic power supply inflates operational costs for service firms and reduces competitiveness</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle">5</div>
    <div class="row-title">Regulatory Burden</div>
    <div class="row-desc">Complex registration, high telecom taxes, and bureaucratic red tape deter formalisation and discourage foreign direct investment</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle brown">6</div>
    <div class="row-title">Informality</div>
    <div class="row-desc">72.1% of non-agricultural workers are informal — shrinking the tax base and leaving most service workers without social protection</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="source-line">Source: Pakistan Economic Survey 2024–25; World Bank June 2025; Mordor Intelligence 2026; PBS Labour Force Survey</div>
```

## Demographics, geography, and digital momentum create a genuine window for services-led growth

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 0.4rem;">
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle">✦</div>
    <div class="row-title">Youth Dividend</div>
    <div class="row-desc">53.8% of Pakistan is working-age (15–59); with the right skills this demographic bulge can power IT, fintech, education, and health services</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle brown">✦</div>
    <div class="row-title">IT & Freelancing</div>
    <div class="row-desc">$3.2 billion in IT exports; English-speaking, young tech talent offers a competitive cost advantage in the $7 trillion global services market</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle">✦</div>
    <div class="row-title">Remittances $32bn</div>
    <div class="row-desc">Remittances grew 11% to $32 billion in FY25 — the largest forex source — sustaining household consumption and retail services demand</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle rust">✦</div>
    <div class="row-title">CPEC Connectivity</div>
    <div class="row-desc">CPEC enhances logistics, transport corridors, and cross-border trade; CPEC-II adds digital and green corridor components</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle">✦</div>
    <div class="row-title">Financial Inclusion</div>
    <div class="row-desc">Mobile wallets (JazzCash: 48mn users) and SBP's digital push can bring millions of unbanked Pakistanis into formal financial services</div>
  </div>
  <div class="icon-row">
    <div class="icon-circle brown">✦</div>
    <div class="row-title">Tourism Potential</div>
    <div class="row-desc">Pakistan's scenic North, cultural heritage sites, and hospitality sector offer significant growth if security and infrastructure improve</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="source-line">Source: Pakistan Economic Survey 2024–25; SBP; Mordor Intelligence; World Bank 2025</div>
```

## Five reforms would unlock the services sector's true potential and make it an engine of inclusive growth

1. **Formalise the Informal:** Simplify business registration, offer tax amnesties, and use digital payment data to bring service providers into the tax net — widening the base without raising rates

2. **Invest in Human Capital:** Raise education spending toward 4–5% of GDP; expand vocational and digital skills training aligned with what services employers actually need

3. **Deepen Financial Inclusion:** Use SBP's digital infrastructure and mobile money platforms to extend credit, insurance, and savings products to the unbanked majority

4. **Reform Telecom Taxation:** Reduce duties on mobile devices and dollar-linked spectrum fees to accelerate 5G rollout, smartphone adoption, and the digital economy

5. **Promote Services Exports:** Strengthen PSEB, invest in IT parks, offer R&D incentives, and negotiate bilateral services trade agreements to capture global market share

::: {.source-line}
Source: IMF Article IV 2024; World Bank Pakistan Development Update 2025; Pakistan Economic Survey 2024–25
:::

## Key Takeaways {background-color="#F7F7F2"}

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 0.5rem;">
  <div class="takeaway-row">
    <div class="tnum">1</div>
    <div>Services account for <strong>58.4% of GDP</strong> and employ <strong>38% of Pakistan's workforce</strong> — making it the single most important sector in the economy today</div>
  </div>
  <div class="takeaway-row">
    <div class="tnum">2</div>
    <div>Wholesale & retail trade (30.8%), transport (18.2%), and real estate (10.1%) are the three largest sub-sectors; <strong>IT/telecom and finance are the fastest-growing</strong></div>
  </div>
  <div class="takeaway-row">
    <div class="tnum">3</div>
    <div>A massive <strong>informal economy — 72% of non-agricultural employment</strong> — is Pakistan's biggest structural challenge: it shrinks the tax base and denies workers social protection</div>
  </div>
  <div class="takeaway-row">
    <div class="tnum">4</div>
    <div>Pakistan's IT sector ($3.2bn exports, 200mn telecom subscribers, 1,900+ incubated startups) is a genuine growth engine <strong>constrained by high taxes, skills gaps, and energy costs</strong></div>
  </div>
  <div class="takeaway-row">
    <div class="tnum">5</div>
    <div>The way forward requires <strong>five parallel reforms:</strong> formalisation, human capital, financial inclusion, telecom tax reduction, and a deliberate services export strategy</div>
  </div>
</div>
```
